svg.title: Copy of RedAlliance_B1: shoot 4, then drive along the side wall to the LOADING ZONE - RED alliance
svg.desc: Top view of the 141.35 by 141.35 inch BIOBUZZ field, audience at the bottom, red alliance on the left. Route red_b1 for the RED alliance, starting in tile B1, with 6 steps: 1 START at (35.0, 9.2, -90 deg); 2 SHOOT 4 at UP cell from (35.0, 9.2, -115 deg); 3 WAIT 4.5 s; 4 DRIVE path1 reverse tangent to 35.8, 90.0; 5 DRIVE path2 reverse tangent to 12.0, 90.0; 6 PARK at (12.0, 90.0, 0 deg). First tip: we shoot the first tip. Estimated 14.5 s, POLLEN balance -4, up to 28 points for our robot; 5 errors and 2 warnings.
svg.text: Copy of RedAlliance_B1: shoot 4, then drive along the side wall to the LOADING ZONE - RED alliance
id red_b1 | start tile B1 | 6 steps | red ink | first tip: we shoot the first tip

g.title: Where a robot facing -90 degrees may be set up (rule G304): the tinted stretches of the own walls. The gaps are the FLOWERS, the LOADING ZONE, the corners and the center line.
g.text: tinted: where this start may stand (G304)

g.title: step 4: DRIVE path1 reverse tangent to 35.8, 90.0 (t = 9.9 to 12.9 s) - line(start, point1).reverseTangent(): shooter-first up the left corridor.

step 5: DRIVE path2 reverse tangent to 12.0, 90.0 (t = 12.9 to 14.5 s) - line(point1, point2).reverseTangent(): the 0 deg heading in the source is ignored; the robot turns to face +x by itself because it drives toward -x backwards.

step 1: START at (35.0, 9.2, -90 deg) (t = 0.0 to 0.0 s) - The OpMode's number, copied. The robot's center of rotation is 9.2 in from the audience wall, but its front edge is 9.77 in ahead of the center, so the real footprint would reach 0.57 in through the wall: place the real robot with its FRONT ON the wall (center 9.77 in out) and change the OpMode's y to match once the center of rotation is measured.

step 2: SHOOT 4 at UP cell from (35.0, 9.2, -115 deg) (t = 0.0 to 5.4 s) - hold(follower, (35.0, 9.2, -115)) then aimAndLaunch(): spin up, feed, waitMs(5000). hold() is an instant command, so the shot really starts without waiting for the turn.

step 6: PARK at (12.0, 90.0, 0 deg) (t = 14.5 to 14.5 s) - The source never says PARK, but this pose is the red LOADING ZONE corner: it overlaps the zone by 4.3 in (the robot reaches 8.9 in to its left, y 98.9; the zone, taken from the CAD tape, starts at y 94.58), deep enough for PARK. With the old 144 in field numbers the zone started at y 96 and this was only 2.9 in.

step 1: START at (35.0, 9.2, -90 deg) (t = 0.0 to 0.0 s) - The OpMode's number, copied. The robot's center of rotation is 9.2 in from the audience wall, but its front edge is 9.77 in ahead of the center, so the real footprint would reach 0.57 in through the wall: place the real robot with its FRONT ON the wall (center 9.77 in out) and change the OpMode's y to match once the center of rotation is measured.

step 2: SHOOT 4 at UP cell from (35.0, 9.2, -115 deg) (t = 0.0 to 5.4 s) - hold(follower, (35.0, 9.2, -115)) then aimAndLaunch(): spin up, feed, waitMs(5000). hold() is an instant command, so the shot really starts without waiting for the turn.
step 3: WAIT 4.5 s (t = 5.4 to 9.9 s) - waitMs(4500) before launcher.stop(): the volley holds the launcher on for 9.5 s in total.
step 4: DRIVE path1 reverse tangent to 35.8, 90.0 (t = 9.9 to 12.9 s) - line(start, point1).reverseTangent(): shooter-first up the left corridor.

step 5: DRIVE path2 reverse tangent to 12.0, 90.0 (t = 12.9 to 14.5 s) - line(point1, point2).reverseTangent(): the 0 deg heading in the source is ignored; the robot turns to face +x by itself because it drives toward -x backwards.

step 6: PARK at (12.0, 90.0, 0 deg) (t = 14.5 to 14.5 s) - The source never says PARK, but this pose is the red LOADING ZONE corner: it overlaps the zone by 4.3 in (the robot reaches 8.9 in to its left, y 98.9; the zone, taken from the CAD tape, starts at y 94.58), deep enough for PARK. With the old 144 in field numbers the zone started at y 96 and this was only 2.9 in.

g.text: Estimated time 14.5 s of the 30.0 s AUTO (placeholder timing) | Our AUTO points: 28 (LEAVE 3, PARK 5, HIVE TIP 20)
POLLEN: hold 4 at start, +0 taken, -4 fired, 0 at the end (balance -4) | Validator: 5 ERROR, 2 WARN

g.title: WARN step 2 [G417] step 2 (SHOOT, the move to its pose): this volley is TIMED (it feeds for 5.0 s whatever happens, it cannot stop when the camera sees the tip) and the HIVE tips with POLLEN 3 of the 4 (3 NECTAR in the cell; a cell tips at 8 POLLEN-equivalents (each POLLEN counts 1, each NECTAR 5/3)), so the last 1 would be launched into a cell that is already tipping down. FIRST's Q&A QA12 lets you add elements to a HIVE that is moving, but G417 allows launching only into an upward-facing CELL and a launch at a rocking HIVE can spoil the tip. Drop launchSeconds() so the volley is gated by the camera (it stops at the tip and keeps the spare), or fire only 3
